story.title: Coast Guard Searches for Missing Medical Evacuation Jet Off Nantucket
story.summary: The U.S. Coast Guard is conducting a search for a Gulfstream medical evacuation jet that lost contact with flight controllers early Saturday morning. The aircraft, which was carrying six people, was en route from Bermuda to Boston when it went missing near Nantucket.

explore_lenses.label: Why is the search focused south of Nantucket?
explore_lenses.title: Last-known area drives air-and-sea response
explore_lenses.summary: The search area is based on the aircraft's last contact during its Bermuda-to-Boston flight, rather than on a confirmed crash location. Local reporting places the effort about 13 nautical miles south of Nantucket.

claims.text: The Coast Guard said the FAA reported loss of contact with the Gulfstream G100 during the overnight flight from Bermuda to Boston, and that air and surface crews were searching off Nantucket.

Nantucket Current reported that the search was about 13 nautical miles south of the island and included Station Brant Point's 47-foot motor lifeboat, an MH-60 helicopter, an HC-144, a C-130 and a cutter.
The search location is an operational starting point based on the available last-known information; it does not by itself establish where the aircraft is or what happened to it.

explore_lenses.label: What does the flight data show—and not show?
explore_lenses.title: A reported descent is not a cause finding
explore_lenses.summary: Public flight-tracking data cited by news outlets indicate a sharp altitude loss before contact ended, but investigators have not determined a cause. Reported timings also vary slightly across early accounts.

claims.text: CBS, citing FlightAware, reported that the aircraft descended from about 24,000 feet to about 11,000 feet before it disappeared from tracking; ABC separately reported a rapid 7,500-foot descent, citing a source familiar with the investigation.

Early reports differed on the time contact was lost: CBS reported about 1 a.m. local time, while ABC reported about 2 a.m. This may reflect differing time references or updates, and neither account provides an official cause determination.
The National Transportation Safety Board said it was gathering information on October 3, but had no further update to share, according to the Associated Press.

explore_lenses.label: Who was aboard, and why is the operator relevant?
explore_lenses.title: The flight was a Canadian-registered medical transfer
explore_lenses.summary: The aircraft was operated as an air ambulance, making the passenger and crew composition central to the case. Officials had described four crew members and two passengers, but had not publicly identified them or specified the passengers' medical circumstances.

claims.text: Bermuda airport operator Skyport said the Canadian-registered aircraft departed L.F. Wade International Airport with four crew members and two passengers; the total aboard was six.
CBS reported that the jet was registered to Latitude Air Ambulance, while ABC identified the aircraft as a Gulfstream G100 Astra SPX operated by the company.
ABC reported that a source familiar with the investigation said no Americans were aboard; that is not an official public identification of the occupants.

story_report.summary: The U.S. Coast Guard is searching waters off Nantucket after the Federal Aviation Administration reported losing contact with a Gulfstream G100 medical-transport jet flying overnight from Bermuda to Boston. Six people were aboard the Canadian-registered aircraft: four crew members and two passengers. Air and surface crews were deployed after contact was lost, while authorities had not announced that the plane, wreckage or any occupants had been found.

sections.heading: Coast Guard Search Off Nantucket
sections.body: The search was reported about 13 nautical miles south of Nantucket and included a 47-foot motor lifeboat from Station Brant Point, an MH-60 helicopter, an HC-144 aircraft, a C-130 and a cutter. The search area reflects available last-known information and does not establish the aircraft’s location or what happened to it. The National Transportation Safety Board said it was gathering information on Oct. 3 but had no further update to share.

sections.heading: Aircraft Tracking and Operator Details
sections.body: CBS, citing FlightAware, reported that the jet descended from about 24,000 feet to about 11,000 feet before disappearing from tracking. ABC separately reported a rapid 7,500-foot descent, citing a source familiar with the investigation. CBS identified the jet as registered to Latitude Air Ambulance, while ABC described it as a Gulfstream G100 Astra SPX operated by the company.

unresolved.text: Authorities had not publicly determined why contact was lost or whether mechanical trouble, weather, crew action or an impact played a role.

The identities of those aboard, the passengers’ medical status and the purpose of the transfer had not been officially released. ABC, citing a source familiar with the investigation, reported that no Americans were aboard.

related_stories.title: Bodycam Footage Released of Luigi Mangione's Arrest
related_stories.summary: Newly released police bodycam footage captures the arrest of Luigi Mangione at a McDonald's in Pennsylvania. The video shows an officer discovering a gun in Mangione's backpack, occurring shortly after the killing of UnitedHealthcare CEO Brian Thompson. Mangione has pleaded guilty to federal charges related to the incident.
